products.name: Halligan Style Forcible Entry; 24 in. OAL
products.summary: The Council version of the Halligan tool is forged in one piece and designed for maximum forcible entry and breaching.
details: The Council version of the TD24 Halligan tool is growing in popularity and designed in collaboration with top forcible entry trainers.

TD24- Tuned and Dressed Halligan is ready to go. Forks thinned out, Gap and Set marks in place. This forcible entry/breaching tool is drop forged in one piece from 4140 alloy steel. Working ends are heat treated for maximum strength, toughness and wear resistance. The fork, pike and pry are designed for leverage and strength. Widths and tapers are intended to allow easy penetration.
features: Overall length is 24 in
Made of .987″ Octagon 4140 steel
Clear Lacquer finish to deter rust
2” Wide offset Adze w/ 30” radial arc and reference line
Squared off shoulders for flat striking surface
Gap between the fork ends for pulling “key-in-knob”
Flat side target for striker/axe
Made in USA.

products.name: FE6-32 Forcible Entry 6lb Flathead Fire Axe with 32 in. Dual Grip Hickory Handle with Marrying Slot
products.summary: FE6-32 6 lb Forcible Entry Flathead Fire Axe with 32 in. Curved Hickory Handle with Marrying Slot
details: 6.0 lbs. Forcible Entry Flathead fireman’s style single bit axe with a 32 in. Dual Grip American hickory handle. Design elements improve performance and usability while helping to reduce fatigue and injury. Used in all manner of municipal fire fighting applications, chopping, battering, door stop, etc. Cutting edge is approximately 5″ in. overall length and the poll is square. This axe will easily pull its weight on the fire-ground and will be an invaluable tool for trainers and student firefighters.
features: Forged 1060 steel. Made in USA.
Forged in slot to marry most popular Halligan tools to create “The Irons”.
Tapered wedge shaped blade allows it to be used a starter wedge and helps capture progress while forcing a door.
Extended poll helps to counter balance the head so that the center of gravity is within the eye/handle. Balanced to lay flat in an open hand so no blade drop or flutter when swinging sideways.
Top of head is flat to stand on its own.
Hand sharpened, tapered bit for cutting.

ANSI Standards call for bit hardness of Rc 45-60, at least ½ inch back from the cutting edge. Council Tool internal standards call for tempered bit hardness of Rc 48-55 and we target 1-1/4 inches from the cutting edge. The poll and eye walls are not hardened and remain in the as forged condition.
32″ Dual Grip hickory handle. Eye section is dried to below 10% moisture content to minimize shrinkage and help prevent loosening.
Axe head is hydraulically seated onto handle and secured with a traditional wooden and steel wedge.
The interior detail of the eye is tapered and allows for a strong mechanical bond. Approximately 1/2″ of the overall length of the handle is removed during assembly.

products.name: NY Style Roof Hook, 4 ft
products.summary: 1" Diameter Steel Tubing, Drop Forged ends featuring Point on Upper Hook and slotted lower hook with Chisel end.
details: By patterning after traditional fire tools, studying popular modifications, and using feedback from seasoned Firefighters, we have taken the NY style Roof-Hook to a new level.
features: Drop-forged high-Carbon steel hook-head and chisel-end.
1 in. diameter DOM (Drawn Over Mandrel) steel tubing for strength and reduced weight.
No rubber or foam grips, so that it can be used out of the box as is, or customized by the end-user/firefighter.
A slot forged into the lower hook, to allow the forks of a traditional Halligan to be married.
The end of the upper hook comes to a point, so that it can be used to break tempered window-glass/auto-glass, or pierce roof decking to add safety and foot support during roof work.

The chisel end and 1” diameter tubing will slide inside the rung of a standard fire ladder, allowing for additional safety and support while during roof work, or allow gear/equipment to be hung off the side of a ladder to keep it safe and off the ground.
Made in USA!

products.name: Lock X-Traction Tool
products.summary: Forcible entry tool used on commercial doors that are expensive, such as large glass entrance doors on store fronts and will give better control and efficiency when pulling rim-cylinders, keyed doorknobs, and dead-bolt locksets.
details: This type of tool is often used on commercial doors that are expensive, such as large glass entrance doors on store fronts. Replacing a $100 lock is less expensive to the property owner than a $3k-10k glass door.

The LXT-24 (24 in. Lock X-traction Tool) will give better control and efficiency when pulling rim-cylinders, keyed doorknobs, and dead-bolt locksets. The curved geometries of the forked head allow for smooth, controlled, cam-action when prying in multiple directions.

The LXT-24 has the capability to grip the outer rim of an outward facing lock cylinder, pry it out and off, so that a screwdriver or other tool can reach into the lock and activate the deadbolt/latch mechanism. The other end of the tool has the same chisel point as our Roof Hook. It can be used to help force a door, open/clear a window, or punch out an exposed lockset from the door.
The LXT-24 will be a complementary tool for our TD30 & TD24 Halligans, as we expand our forcible entry line of tools.
features: Designed for storefronts and commercial doors, protects expensive glass by targeting the lock. (Cheaper to replace a $100 lock than a $10,000 door.)

Chisel end punches locks, forces doors, or clears windows.

details: Thought to have been developed in the early 1900’s by Edward Pulaski, a legendary Forest Service Ranger in Idaho. It is said that in August, 1910 his presence saved the lives of 45 men during a difficult time in a large fire. A traditional style bit axe blade on one end and a mattock blade for digging or grubbing on the other end. Used in a variety of settings including forestry and general landscaping.
features: Forged from 1060 steel. Made in USA.

ANSI Standards call for bit hardness of Rc 45-60, at least ½ inch back from the cutting edge. Council Tool internal standards call for tempered bit hardness of Rc 48-55.
Body coated with red enamel and the cutting edges in clear lacquer to deter rust.
36 in. double bit American hickory handle. Eye section is dried to below 10% moisture content to minimize shrinkage and help prevent loosening.

Axe head is hydraulically seated onto handle and secured with a serrated aluminum wedge. The serrated shape improves bite and the aluminum choice of material is strong, lightweight and does not change size with moisture content.
The interior detail of the eye is tapered and allows for a strong mechanical bond. A portion of the overall length of the handle is removed during assembly. OAL is nominal.

products.name: Rhino Tool; Solid Shank 38 in. Handle
products.summary: The Rhino Tool is forged from a single piece of high carbon steel.
details: The Rhino Tool is a traditional Wildland firefighting tool developed by USFS Wildland Hotshots.

They would cut apart a forest fire shovel and fabricate it into a large earth moving hoe. This would include cutting off the lower end of the spade, separating the spade from the steel shank/neck and welding it back together at a 90 deg. angle.

Our version of this tool is produced similarly to the NFES Fire shovel, forged as one-piece, into the shape of a hoe, with no welds. This process replaces the need to fabricate/weld, and makes for a more durable tool.
This Rhino Tool comes with a curved primary edge for scraping the ground or digging, and two straight secondary edges used to cut through vegetation, or root systems.
It is available with two different handle lengths, which include the traditional shovel handle 38”, and a longer 48” version.
The overall lengths are approximately 45” & 53” respectively.
